overall: The AG found the Commissioners violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the posting date and time from a meeting notice and by missing the complaint response deadline, but found no intentional violation and declined the earlier allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commissioners' March 19, 2015 meeting notice did not record the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: Here, there is no dispute that the Commissioners failed to indicate the date and time that the notice was posted, as required by law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commissioners' failure to indicate the posting time was intentional because they proceeded after being told the notice was deficient.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we do not find an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Commissioners did not respond to the complaint within 14 business days of receipt, and did not request an extension.
allegations.key_passage: This failure to respond in a timely manner violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised two earlier alleged violations from early 2015 in the complaint's footnote, which were not formally alleged.
allegations.key_passage: Because the only violation formally alleged in the complaint is the allegation concerning the March 19, 2015 meeting notice, we decline to consider these earlier allegations.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
